summary: Backend-only test of new GET /api/matrix/feed?ufc=1 param (UFC card support). Created /app/backend/tests/test_matrix_feed_ufc.py with 6 pytest cases covering: ufc=1 returns top-level 'ufc' key, ufc=0/omitted returns {ok:0}, no regression on flight/score/scores/alert/temp keys when combined with flights=1&sports=1&weather=1&ufc=1, no 500 errors, and cache key differentiation between ufc=0 and ufc=1 requests. All 6 tests passed (100%).
critical_code_review_comments: _fetch_ufc and matrix_feed correctly handle non-200 ESPN responses and exceptions by returning {ok:0}, satisfying the 'graceful failure, no 500' requirement.

Cache key in matrix_feed (f"{lat},{lon},{radius},{team},{severity},{flights}{sports}{weather}{ufc}") correctly includes ufc as a distinguishing digit, so ufc=0 vs ufc=1 requests are cached separately - verified empirically (no stale cross-contamination observed).

NOTE: Could not verify the ok:1 / real-data path for _fetch_ufc in this sandbox: direct curl to https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/mma/ufc/scoreboard from this environment returns HTTP 403 'Access Denied' (Akamai edge block, likely datacenter/proxy IP block by ESPN), so both direct curl and the backend's own httpx call receive non-200 and correctly fall back to {ok:0}. This is an ESPN-side network restriction in this sandbox, not a backend code bug - the fallback behavior is exactly what the spec requires for that case. Could not confirm the ok:1 shape (name/date/headline non-empty) against a live real event because of this outbound restriction; code review of the ok:1 branch (name/date/headline construction) looks correct and matches the required response shape.
